title: Refactor Profile Dialog and Profile Model
description:
Greatly improve the flexibility of the profile model.  The persistent data is still stored at the UI layer, but now only has a single list of profiles and the ProfileModel is what handles the changes only while in the Profile Dialog.  Other clients of the ProfileModel really just wanted the list of profiles and the active one in a Qt object friendly format, so provide that.  The ProfileDialog is modal, so there shouldn't be concurrency issues with the data.

There are slight changes to the "bookkeeping" of the profiles while in the dialog, hopefully all for the better.
1. Changes are only accepted/written if OK button is clicked.
2. Deleted profiles are marked as such until the dialog closes.
3. Renaming a deleted profile will "undelete" it (within the dialog)
4. Multiple imports in the same ProfileDialog "session" are now supported.

Also started integrating profiles into the "UI init", so that they only need to be retrieved once (in one place) at startup.
Made "profile UI API" consistently start with the profile_ prefix

Fixes #16504

AI-Assisted: no

The first big issue I find is that the profile list is out of sync and not updated.
1. Adding a new folder in the profiles directory is not reflected in Wireshark without a restart
2. Renaming a profile is not updated in the dialog list or the status bar popup menu
3. Renaming the same profile again gives an "Can't rename directory" error

The use case is an external installer which adds a extcap binary with a corresponding profile. We must not force a Wireshark restart to use the new profile. This was one of the main design goals when I made the profile support. Reading the directory structure must be the only way to list profiles, no caching.
QFileSystemWatcher might be useful in this case.

There have been discussions about the ui/ folder and how a lot of it could be removed for "full Qt functionality".  I'm not yet ready to go there with some of the current profile functionality, mostly because I still want the potential to share code with TShark (looking at some open issues with "profile" search).  So, while you may be right about using QFileSystemWatcher, I don't plan to put it in the current MR.  I'm just trying to clean up the problems mentioned in #16504 and provide a better interface.  I originally thought this MR could help out preference handling (!23215), but that may be a case where "full Qt solution" is more warranted (and also achievable with these changes)
Sorry that I completely missed "syncing" the profiles the first time.  That has been addressed.

1. Issues with the hintLabel
 * Rename
   * Rename a profile does not update the hintLabel, it's still the old path.
   * Select a different profile and then back to the renamed profile will update the hintLabel.
   * The link of the "Renamed from:" open a different profile.
   * Rename the profile back to the original name, it's still the "Renamed from" label.
   * Select a different profile and then back to the renamed profile now has a blank hintLabel.
 * Delete
   * The link of the "A profile with this name is being deleted" open a folder for the last selected profile (or the default). This should either open the folder for the deleted profile or not have a link.
   * The hintLabel should contain the profile name being deleted, not a generic "A profile with this name".
   * Deleting the Default profile does not reflect it will be reset to default.

2. Deleting a profile does not immediately mark the entry as deleted, I must select a different profile to update UI. Pressing Ok with the deleted profile selected will delete the profile directory but it's still being used and saving preferences will silently create the profile again.

3. The "Copy this profile" button is disabled.

4. Create a few new profiles and then delete the first of them causes update issues in the list.

I will continue testing after you have fixed this issues. Please do more sanity checking. I do not want to end up in the same situation as with the faulty refactoring in 2019 when I used a week testing and reporting bugs.
All of the aforementioned bugs should now be fixed.  Several of them exposed some "event handling" that needed to be done better (where one code fix handled several bugs)

5. Delete the profile in use. Pressing Ok with the deleted profile selected will delete the profile directory but it's still being used and saving preferences will silently create the profile again. Open the profiles dialog will show no selected profile.
6. Delete a profile. Keep the deleted profile selected and press the button to add a new profile. Nothing visually happens, but in the background the profile is undeleted. Select a different profile to update the visual (profile no longer shown as deleted).
7. Delete a profile. The profile name gets a strikethrough but the type or auto-switch-filter does not. Select a different profile will update the visual.
8. Add a new profile. Close the profiles dialog and open it again. The created profile is in the bottom of the list and not in the alphabetically sorted (personal) list.

I will continue testing after you have fixed this issues.

10. Add a new profile. The created profile is in the bottom of the popup list (lower right corner) and not in the alphabetically sorted list.
11. Use a profile different from Default. When having a deleted profile (not the one in use) selected when pressing OK the profile in use should be kept, not changed to Default.
12. When deleting a profile the selection should not move to the profile in use, but stay on the deleted profile. This will make it equal behavior when deleting the profile in use and when deleting another profile.

You can already see the "status" of the profile by the fact that it has a strikethrough, so I didn't think the "note" at the bottom needed to duplicate it (but didn't have other ideas for the text). I can agree on number 22, we can keep this.

17. I like the 4.6.x hint label better because it has a reference to the conflicting profile. From the example, let's say you rename "Two" to "Three" and then "One" to "Two". For "Two" it would be good to have a reference to "Three" because this will show the rename.

24. Press OK in case 23. Observe the profile is not deleted.
What do you think the intended behavior should be here (23-24)?  Delete the profile under the old name? Not allow a renamed profile to be deleted in that session of the dialog?

I went with making a flag for deleted profiles rather than have it be a state.  So now a profile can be renamed (state) and deleted (flag) so the "original name" profile will be deleted if it is renamed and then deleted.
24. The renamed profile is still not deleted.
Did you have a look how to improve the hint label in case 17.? It's still the generic hint label.

I think it's a very valid test case and certainly the "simplified version" (I could see a user ending up in this scenario after more complicated changes).  But I'm also fine with the fact that the user can't accept the profiles as is (OK is disabled), so they have to "back out and try again" with the Cancel button.  There is no longer an error message displayed (because OK button is disabled).

When thinking about it, it's not impossible to implement copy to a temp folder. Or use a popup error to prevent duplicate profile names. Or find a solution to the other issues.

We should use the knowledge from this refactoring to list all cases which gives a disabled "Ok" button. Then we find a solution to either prevent them from happening or handle them correctly. No need to do it in this MR, but it would improve the UX.

Ok, let's close this advent calendar and create action points in a new Work item.

At this point, I think this is worth merging so others can evaluate it.  @stigbjorlykke you've been a tremendous help, with edge cases I don't think I would have come up with on my own.  And while a few more edge cases may remain, the overall feature seems stable.  And if issues arrive, add a note here or assign me a new issue.  I'm not going anywhere.
This is my fear with this refactoring. Not many others will evaluate it and new issues may only be found after release. Unless we do thorough testing before merge.

But without the refactoring, it's hard to more forward and add additional features (which is where I was really trying to get to, but wasn't going to cloud this MR with unnecessary enhancements).  I don't have strong opinions on this being in 4.7 or 5.0, but I thought we had a development branch for a reason.  There is a wider net of people using the development (master) branch than testing individual MRs and I think it's ready enough for that.

Don't get me wrong, I like refactoring for improvement. This one will hopefully make it easier to implement hierarchical profiles, which has been a wish for some years. But for this dialog specifically history has shown that it's hard to change without introducing a lot of bugs, just ask @rknall.

As I already have stated, many of the use cases leading to bugs here is not common, but because it's possible it should not give wrong behavior. I think we are very close now so let's aim for the 4.7 release.
Sounds good!
marked this merge request as **ready**
Having a list of names where a user can add, rename, copy and delete, should not be an uncommon use case. Maybe we should look for other similar implementations how to solve this.

Are you thinking within the Wireshark code base itself or have "AI assistance" do the refactor because [CRUD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Create,_read,_update_and_delete) is a fairly popular operation and AI should be able to "acquire" code from what it's learned on the interwebs.  I thought there was enough nuance with integration in the Wireshark code base, that I'm not sure AI is quite ready (and would probably reintroduce bugs you've already found)

I'm not thinking about anything specific, I'm just thinking that it should be possible to mimic other implementations for add/rename/copy/delete like we do here. The hint label is heavily used and I think we should keep that. For item 17. I think we should use the hint label as we do in 4.6.
Next version will have it behaving like 4.6.

Just fyi - "Make the profile data more "Qt native-like" (seems it wasn't fully converted from the GTK days)" That sentence is not correct. The initial idea was to avoid the massive over engineering and just focus on a better experience in the handling of the dialog and the models. And that was achieved. From a Qt POV, the model hides the implementation. That is exactly what the previous implementation did. It is true that most examples use an internal *Item something to store the elements, but that is neither a requirement nor a Qt necessity. One could even argue, that instead of rewriting the model, one could rewrite ui/profile.? which would make more sense in my opinion. This way we just add another layer of ambiguity between the GTK world and the Qt world that is strictly speaking not required. Some parts are more elegant in this solution, absolutely and I am overall not against it.

The original goal was to completely replace ui/profile. and move it all into the model, but that didn't quite allow for maximum code reuse (with say things like tshark), at least for this iteration.  Yes, I consider all of "ui/profile." to be from the GTK days and that's what the statement was referencing.  I could change it to just "improved profile model" because you're right that this MR didn't "create" the model implementation.
